title: Abdominal Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Episodic pain — may appear well between episodes.
rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Sausage-shaped mass in RLQ. Episodic pain with drawing up of knees.
rationale.Abdominal ultrasound: Target/doughnut sign. Diagnostic test of choice.
rationale.Abdominal X-ray: Rule out perforation (free air) before enema. May show signs of obstruction.
rationale.Air/contrast enema: Therapeutic reduction. 80-90% success. Do NOT attempt if perforation.
rationale.Pediatric surgery consult: If enema fails or perforation → surgical reduction.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a child (commonly 6 months - 3 years) presenting with acute severe colicky abdominal pain occurring in episodes, with drawing up of knees, and currant jelly stools (blood and mucus). Between episodes the child may appear normal. A sausage-shaped mass may be palpable in the RLQ (intussusception of terminal ileum into cecum — most common type). Intussusception is the most common cause of intestinal obstruction in children <2 years. Peak incidence 6-12 months. Often preceded by viral illness (rotavirus, adenovirus). Diagnostic test of choice: abdominal ultrasound (target sign/doughnut sign on transverse view). Treatment: therapeutic air or contrast enema (reduces the intussusception in 80-90%). Do NOT attempt enema if perforation (free air on X-ray). Surgical reduction if enema fails or perforation present. NPO and NG tube for decompression. IV fluids for resuscitation.
